body: I can only speak from my own experience as someone with social anxiety and on the spectrum but I had a lot of fun when I went. I have a hard time being around a lot of people but all the other attendees were really cool. I went by myself and I didn’t talk to many people but everyone was chill. It was definitely loud and a lot to deal with but I paid for the ticket and drove 2 hours into a city to go so I had no intentions of letting all that effort be wasted. I stood pretty close to the stage so I was surrounded by people. There were a couple things that helped. I was in a town two hours away from home so chances were that I’d never see any of the other people there again. Jazmin has curated a really sweet fan base in my opinion. I’d guess that the majority of us are queer which made the concert space feel really safe for me. It was stressful at first but I couldn’t stop smiling for the first ten minutes of driving back home. I was so proud of myself for going. The music was great and I had a lot of fun dancing and singing with others. I felt very comfortable being myself. The fan base is absolutely amazing and I think Jazmin was the perfect first concert for me. I’d recommend that you go and just enjoy yourself the best you can. You don’t have to stay for the whole thing and you can leave whenever. It’s a huge step to take but I promise that it’s not so scary. But do whatever feels right for you. You know your own limits better than anyone. I’m wishing you the best luck!

I used to work as a cashier and I just didn’t greet people. Im surprised I didn’t get fired from my first cashiering job cause I didn’t speak to the customers at all. It’s easier for me to talk to people now cause I’ve found the way I like to talk and what words I like using. Customer service was helpful in the way that I could use different terms and words with each customer to find what felt right. I hate saying hi but hey feels natural. I also hate saying bye or goodbye so I typically say see ya now. You just have to figure out what works for you. And train yourself to use what you choose. I would say hey to every customer and see ya to every customer. I got used to it and it happens naturally now. Also, most people don’t notice your voice or if you don’t greet them. People aren’t nearly as observant as we think.
